x.ASV: In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for uncleanness.
x.Darby: In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness.
x.KJV: In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness.
x.YLT: In that day there is a fountain opened To the house of David And to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, For sin and for impurity.

nt: Zechariah is using the phrase **On that day** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event. See the Introduction to Zechariah for a discussion of the similar phrase “in that day.”

Here Zechariah is speaking as if the means of cleansing from sin were a **fountain** that would **be opened**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a source of cleansing will be made available]

The expression **a fountain will be opened** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [God will open a fountain]

Here, **the house of David** represents the descendants of David and the royal dynasty. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people descended from David]

Zechariah is referring to all types of uncleanness by naming two major components, sin and impurity. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [every kind of sin and ritual uncleanness]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of sin and impurity, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [cleansing you from your sinning and from your being unclean]

t: I will cause to pass away

x.ASV: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith Jehovah of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered; and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land.
x.Darby: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith Jehovah of hosts, [that] I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered; and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land.
x.KJV: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered: and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land.
x.YLT: And it hath come to pass, in that day, An affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts, I cut off the names of the idols from the land, And they are not remembered any more, And also the prophets and the spirit of uncleanness I cause to pass away from the land.

nt: Here, **the names of the idols** represents the memory and reputation of the idols. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the memory of the idols]

The phrase **the declaration of Yahweh of Armies** is a parenthetical statement within Yahweh’s speech that identifies him as the speaker. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating the speaker of a direct quotation in your language.

The expression **they will not be remembered again** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one will remember them anymore]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of uncleanness, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what is unclean]

Here, the words **and also** add a further action to the one just described. Yahweh will not only remove the idols but will additionally remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [and furthermore,]

t: and/ they will pierce through/ him

x.ASV: And it shall come to pass that, when any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of Jehovah; and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.
x.Darby: And it shall come to pass, if any shall yet prophesy, that his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of Jehovah; and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.
x.KJV: And it shall come to pass, that when any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of the Lord: and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.
x.YLT: And it hath been, when one prophesieth again, That said unto him have his father and his mother, his parents, `Thou dost not live, For falsehood thou hast spoken in the name of Jehovah,' And pierced him through have his father and his mother, his parents, in his prophesying.

nt: Zechariah is presenting a possible condition, that a man will prophesy falsely again and, as a result, his own father and mother will condemn and kill him. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement is first. Alternate translation: [If a man prophesies falsely again]

Zechariah is not referring to a specific **man**. He means men in general who prophesy. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [any man] or [anyone]

Zechariah is not distinguishing this father and mother from another father and mother who are not **the ones bearing him**. He is reminding readers that the man’s own parents are the ones who gave birth to him. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [who themselves gave him birth]
לֹ֣א תִֽחְיֶ֔ה כִּ֛י שֶׁ֥קֶר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ בְּ⁠שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה

The father and mother’s words are a quotation within a quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that he will not live, for he has spoken falsehood in the name of Yahweh]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **falsehood**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you have spoken falsely]

Here, **the name of Yahweh** represents the authority of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [as one who has Yahweh’s authority]

x.ASV: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision, when he prophesieth; neither shall they wear a hairy mantle to deceive:
x.Darby: And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision, when he prophesieth; neither shall they wear a hairy mantle to deceive.
x.KJV: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision, when he hath prophesied; neither shall they wear a rough garment to deceive:
x.YLT: And it hath come to pass, in that day, Ashamed are the prophets, each of his vision, in his prophesying, And they put not on a hairy robe to deceive.

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **shame**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the prophets will be ashamed]

The implication is that a **cloak of hair** was the distinctive garment that prophets wore, so putting it on was a way of claiming to be a prophet. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the hairy cloak that marks a person as a prophet]

x.ASV: but he shall say, I am no prophet, I am a tiller of the ground; for I have been made a bondman from my youth.
x.Darby: And he shall say, I am no prophet, I am a tiller of the ground; for man acquired me [as bondman] from my youth.
x.KJV: But he shall say, I am no prophet, I am an husbandman; for man taught me to keep cattle from my youth.
x.YLT: And one hath said, `I am not a prophet, A man, a tiller of ground I am, For ground is my possession from my youth.'

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **youth**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [since I was a boy]

This could mean: (1) that the person is tied to this land and working this land because he is a bondservant or slave to the owner. Alternate translation: [this ground that my master from my youth owns] (2) that he owns this land (requires reading the Hebrew slightly differently). That is, he’s a small landowner or a subsistence farmer and is tied to the land. Alternate translation: [the little patch of ground I have owned since I was young]

x.ASV: And one shall say unto him, What are these wounds between thine arms? Then he shall answer, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.
x.Darby: And one shall say unto him, What are those wounds in thy hands? And he will say, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.
x.KJV: And one shall say unto him, What are these wounds in thine hands? Then he shall answer, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.
x.YLT: And one hath said unto him, `What are these wounds in thy hands?' And he hath said, `Because I was smitten at home by my lovers.'

nt: וְ⁠אָמַ֣ר אֵלָ֔י⁠ו מָ֧ה הַ⁠מַּכּ֛וֹת הָ⁠אֵ֖לֶּה בֵּ֣ין יָדֶ֑י⁠ךָ וְ⁠אָמַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכֵּ֖יתִי בֵּ֥ית מְאַהֲבָֽ⁠י

The question and its answer here are quotations within a quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And someone will ask him what those wounds between his hands are. And he will say that those are the ones with which he was struck in the house of his lovers]

The speaker is using **between your hands** as a common expression of the culture to mean “on the front of the body.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [on the front of your body]

The expression **I was struck** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people struck me]

This could mean: (1) that the speaker is saying he was injured somehow while at the home of friends, perhaps in a drunken brawl or something. Alternate translation: [when I got in a fight with some local people] (2) that the speaker is speaking of the false gods that he worshiped as if they were his **lovers**. Idol worship sometimes involves self-mutilation. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the temples of the false gods I worshiped]

x.ASV: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Jehovah of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered; and I will turn my hand upon the little ones.
x.Darby: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, even against the man [that is] my fellow, saith Jehovah of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered, and I will turn my hand upon the little ones.
x.KJV: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the Lord of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.
x.YLT: Sword, awake against My shepherd, And against a hero--My fellow, An affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts. Smite the shepherd, and scattered is the flock, And I have put back My hand on the little ones.

nt: Yahweh is speaking to a **Sword** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the judgment that is coming on his shepherd. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the sword. Alternate translation: [May the sword awake against my shepherd]

**Sword, awake against my shepherd, and against the man, my companion**—Yahweh is using the term **Sword** to represent the violent death that a sword can inflict. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Someone, kill my shepherd with a sword]

Zechariah is using **the declaration of Yahweh of Armies** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

Yahweh is speaking of the leader of his people as if he were a **shepherd**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the leader of my people … the leader of my people]

Yahweh is speaking of his people as if they were a **flock** of sheep. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and my people will scatter]

Here, **hand** represents the power of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will use my power against]

Yahweh is using the adjective **little ones** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person, those who are lowly and insignificant. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the ones who are insignificant]

x.ASV: And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith Jehovah, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.
x.Darby: And it shall come to pass in all the land, saith Jehovah, two parts therein shall be cut off [and] die; but the third shall be left therein.
x.KJV: And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.
x.YLT: And it hath come to pass, In all the land, an affirmation of Jehovah, Two parts in it are cut off--they expire, And the third is left in it.

nt: פִּֽי־שְׁנַ֣יִם בָּ֔⁠הּ יִכָּרְת֖וּ יִגְוָ֑עוּ וְ⁠הַ⁠שְּׁלִשִׁ֖ית יִוָּ֥תֶר בָּֽ⁠הּ

The expression **two portions** means two parts out of three equal parts, that is, two-thirds of the people. And **the third** means one part out of three equal parts, that is, one-third of the people.

The expression **will be cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will cut off two portions in it]

Yahweh is speaking of people being killed as if they were parts of something that could be **cut off**, such as cutting branches from a tree. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will be killed]

Yahweh is speaking of the people who will die as if their lives were a breath that will **expire**, or run out. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [breathe their last breath] or [die]

The expression **will be left** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and I will leave the third in it]

x.ASV: And I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried. They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people; and they shall say, Jehovah is my God.
x.Darby: And I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried. They shall call on my name, and I will answer them: I will say, It is my people; and they shall say, Jehovah is myGod.
x.KJV: And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.
x.YLT: And I have brought the third into fire, And refined them like a refining of silver, And have tried them like a trying of gold, It doth call in My name, and I answer it, I have said, `My people it is,' And it saith, `Jehovah is my God!'

nt: Yahweh is speaking of the suffering he will use to purify his people as if it were a **fire**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will bring the third through purifying suffering]
וּ⁠צְרַפְתִּי⁠ם֙ כִּ⁠צְרֹ֣ף אֶת־הַ⁠כֶּ֔סֶף וּ⁠בְחַנְתִּ֖י⁠ם כִּ⁠בְחֹ֣ן אֶת־הַ⁠זָּהָ֑ב

The point of this comparison is that just as one **refines the silver** and **tests the gold** to remove impurities and prove them genuine, so Yahweh will purify his people through suffering and prove that they are genuine. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and I will purify them the way that one refines silver to remove its impurities, and I will prove them genuine the way that one tests gold]
The pronoun **He** refers to the surviving third of the people. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The surviving third, they]

Yahweh is stating the pronouns **He** and **I** along with the verbs translated as **he will call** and **I will answer**, which already include their meanings. He is doing that because he is contrasting what the remnant of his people will do with what he himself will do. If a speaker of your language would use explicit pronouns for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that meaning here. Alternate translation: [As for them, they will call on my name, and as for me, I will answer him]

Yahweh is using **call on my name** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to worship me and pray to me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he will worship me and pray to me]

The implication is that **He is my people** and **Yahweh is my God** are the words of a covenant, expressing the restored relationship in which Yahweh claims these people as his own and they acknowledge him as their God. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [He is the people I claim as my own … Yahweh is the one I acknowledge as my God]
עַמִּ֣⁠י ה֔וּא וְ⁠ה֥וּא יֹאמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽ⁠י

There are quotations within a quotation here. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that he is my people, and he, he will say that Yahweh is his God]
